children: Palm oil ended higher. Prices were supported by bargain hunting following the recent sharp selloff, according to David Ng, a trader at Kuala Lumpur-based Iceberg X. That was despite continuing concerns about elevated Malaysian inventories and sluggish export demand, he adds. Ng expects prices to have support around 4,080 ringgit a ton and face resistance at 4,250 ringgit a ton. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for February delivery rose 99 ringgit to 4,240 ringgit a ton. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)
